source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Which command produced the position shown by the calibrated stage?
meaning: An inverse function reverses a one-to-one rule by exchanging its inputs and outputs. For an affine calibration, subtract the offset and divide by the nonzero gain. The inverse is a function, rather than the reciprocal of a function value. Here a nonzero affine gain makes the rule a one-to-one function from the real line onto the real line, so every observed position has one recovered command.

definition.setting: A workshop positioning stage accepts a signed command x in centimetres. Its declared calibration reports position y=ax+b in centimetres. After observing y, a technician removes the zero offset b, then divides by gain a to recover the command. A negative gain means the coordinate axis is reversed.
conditions: The affine rule has domain and range all real numbers for nonzero a. This demonstration bounds y to [−8,8] cm and b to [−3,3] cm, with gain a in [−3,3] and |a| at least 0.25. The inverse domain is the original range; its inverse range is the original domain. The calibration is declared, not fitted to measurements. Numerical round trips approximate the exact algebraic identity. A nonzero recovered command that underflows is reported as a precision failure.
